open_points.subject: issuing a viewer credential after viewer revocation
open_points.text: “Created/modified by: administrator only (R0-14): issue, re-issue and revocation.” The text does not say whether issue or re-issue requires the ClientViewer to be active.
open_points.question: May an administrator issue a new ViewerAccessCredential for a terminally revoked ClientViewer?
options: Refuse issuance because the viewer is revoked.
Create a non-revoked credential, which remains unusable because the viewer is revoked.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse issuance for a revoked viewer.

witness.initial: Viewer V is revoked and has no non-revoked credential.
events: An administrator issues a new access link for V.
outcomes: The action is refused and no ViewerAccessCredential is created.
A new non-revoked ViewerAccessCredential and one-time secret are created, but entry cannot produce an active session while V remains revoked.
witness.observer: The administrator sees either rejection or a newly issued secret and credential.

open_points.subject: granting a project to a revoked viewer
open_points.text: “Created/modified by: administrator only (R0-14).” The creation rules constrain the project lifecycle and pair uniqueness but do not say whether the target viewer must be active.
open_points.question: May an administrator create a ProjectViewerGrant whose ClientViewer is already revoked?
options: Require an active viewer and refuse the grant.
Allow creation of an active but currently unusable grant for the revoked viewer.
open_points.default_guess: Require the target viewer to be active.

witness.initial: Viewer V is revoked, active Registry project P exists, and no grant for (V,P) has ever existed.
events: An administrator grants P to V.
outcomes: No grant is created because V is revoked.
An active ProjectViewerGrant is created, although V cannot use it.
witness.observer: The administrator and subsequent grant listings see whether the grant exists.

open_points.subject: staff sign-out-everywhere
open_points.text: State 0 promises “managed sessions with expiry, revocation, and sign-out-everywhere,” while M06 says sessions are revoked by “logout (that session), an administrator revoking all sessions of an account, the holder's own password change (every other session of the account), and suspension/disabling.”
open_points.question: Can a staff holder explicitly revoke all of their own sessions without changing their password, or is all-session revocation administrator-only?
options: Provide a holder-initiated sign-out-everywhere action that revokes every session, including the current one.
Provide only current-session logout for the holder; only an administrator or another listed event can revoke all sessions.
open_points.default_guess: Provide holder-initiated sign-out-everywhere to satisfy State 0.

witness.initial: Staff member S has active sessions A and B.
events: Through session A, S requests sign-out-everywhere without changing the password.
outcomes: A and B are both revoked.
No such holder action exists, or only A is revoked by ordinary logout while B remains active.
witness.observer: S sees whether session B can still authenticate.

open_points.subject: re-enabling a disabled service principal
open_points.text: Meaning says “the only modification is the status change `active ↔ disabled`,” but Lifecycle candidate says “`active → disabled`.”
open_points.question: Is `disabled` terminal, or may an administrator return a ServicePrincipal to `active`?
options: Disabled is terminal.
An administrator may re-enable a disabled principal.
open_points.default_guess: Treat disabled as terminal unless an explicit re-enable lifecycle is specified.

witness.initial: ServicePrincipal S is active and then disabled; its existing credentials are revoked.
events: An administrator attempts to change S back to active.
outcomes: The action is refused because disabled is terminal.
S becomes active again and can receive or use newly issued credentials.
witness.observer: The administrator and producer see whether S can operate again.

open_points.subject: issuing credentials for a disabled principal
open_points.text: “Created/modified by: administrator.” and “a disabled principal invalidates all of them” do not say whether a new credential may be issued while the principal is disabled.
open_points.question: May an administrator create or rotate a ServiceCredential for a currently disabled ServicePrincipal?
options: Refuse issuance until the principal is active.
Create the credential, but keep it unusable while the principal is disabled.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse credential issuance for a disabled principal.

witness.initial: ServicePrincipal S is disabled and has no valid credentials.
events: An administrator requests a new credential for S.
outcomes: No credential is created.
A new credential, key version and one-time secret are created, although authentication remains blocked while S is disabled.
witness.observer: The administrator sees either rejection or the new one-time secret.

open_points.subject: granting a project to a disabled producer
open_points.text: The model says a grant is “consulted only when the principal's `scope_mode` is `granted_projects`,” but gives no required status for the target ServicePrincipal when a grant is created.
open_points.question: May an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a disabled ServicePrincipal?
options: Require the target principal to be active.
Allow an active grant to be created while the principal is disabled.
open_points.default_guess: Require the target principal to be active.

witness.initial: Disabled ServicePrincipal S has `scope_mode = granted_projects`; active Registry project P exists; the pair has no earlier grant.
events: An administrator grants P to S.
outcomes: The grant is refused because S is disabled.
An active ProducerProjectGrant is created and becomes effective if S can later become active.
witness.observer: The administrator and producer-grant listings see whether the grant exists.

open_points.subject: grants for an all-projects producer
open_points.text: M13 says an `all_projects` principal admits imports without consulting a grant, while M15 only says grants are “consulted only when the principal's `scope_mode` is `granted_projects`”; it does not say whether creation of an unused grant is allowed.
open_points.question: May an administrator create ProducerProjectGrant records for a principal whose scope mode is `all_projects`?
options: Refuse such grants because they can never affect authorization.
Allow them as persisted but authorization-irrelevant records.

witness.initial: Active ServicePrincipal S has `scope_mode = all_projects`; active Registry project P exists.
events: An administrator attempts to grant P to S.
outcomes: The action is refused and no grant exists.
An active ProducerProjectGrant is stored but never consulted.
witness.observer: The administrator sees whether a grant record is created.

open_points.subject: creation of the manual BudgetVersion
open_points.text: The model says “at most one manual version per project,” while M21 and M23 say a manual section and plan are created by an upsert; no passage says which action creates the containing manual BudgetVersion when none exists.
open_points.question: What product action creates a project's first manual BudgetVersion?
options: The first manual-section upsert lazily creates the manual BudgetVersion and its first section and plan atomically.
A separate explicit budget-version creation action must run before section upserts.
Some project-onboarding action creates an empty manual BudgetVersion in advance.
open_points.default_guess: Create it atomically on the first manual-section upsert.

witness.initial: Active project P has no BudgetVersion, PortalSection or SectionPlan.
events: An authorized operator upserts P's first manual section without a section_id.
outcomes: The upsert creates a manual BudgetVersion plus the PortalSection and SectionPlan.
The upsert is refused until another action creates the manual BudgetVersion, or the version already had to exist from onboarding.
witness.observer: The operator sees whether the first section upsert succeeds and which records appear.

open_points.subject: reactivating a previously deactivated budget version
open_points.text: The lifecycle is written as “`inactive → active → inactive`,” while the rules say activation of one version deactivates the previous one and that deactivated versions are never deleted; they do not state whether the final inactive state may transition to active again.
open_points.question: Can a previously deactivated BudgetVersion be activated again?
options: Yes; any inactive version may be activated repeatedly.
No; once deactivated, a version remains historical and terminally inactive.
open_points.default_guess: Treat a deactivated version as terminally inactive because the stated lifecycle has one activation cycle.

witness.initial: Project P has version V1 deactivated after V2 was activated.
events: An authorized staff member attempts to activate V1 again.
outcomes: V1 becomes active and V2 is deactivated.
The action is refused because V1 has already completed its lifecycle.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers see which budget version is active.

open_points.subject: replay outcome stored in ExpenseAggregate
open_points.text: Meaning lists “`replayed: bool`” as an ExpenseAggregate field, while Carried changes says “the aggregate no longer carries `replayed`; the replay outcome travels in a separate operation outcome beside the aggregate.”
open_points.question: Does ExpenseAggregate contain the `replayed` fact, or is that fact present only in ExpenseOperationOutcome?
options: Keep `replayed` on ExpenseAggregate.
Remove it from ExpenseAggregate and expose it only through ExpenseOperationOutcome.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the accepted carried change and keep `replayed` only in ExpenseOperationOutcome.

witness.initial: Expense E already exists from a prior intake.
events: A staff member submits an equal-fingerprint replay and receives the operation result.
outcomes: The returned ExpenseAggregate itself has `replayed=true`.
The aggregate has no replay field; a separate ExpenseOperationOutcome carries `replayed=true`.
witness.observer: The calling module or API mapper sees a different result model.

open_points.subject: same intake_id with different photo content
open_points.text: The only replay rule is “replay of one `intake_id` never duplicates”; it does not say what happens when the same `intake_id` is presented with different `file_ref`, project, date, section, caption or visibility.
open_points.question: How is a ProgressPhoto publication with an existing `intake_id` but different content classified, and may it change the existing photo?
options: Treat it as an integrity conflict and change nothing.
Return the existing photo as a replay regardless of differing content.
Apply some or all differing fields as an update to the existing photo.
open_points.default_guess: Treat differing content under the same intake_id as an integrity conflict that changes nothing.

witness.initial: Photo F exists from intake_id I with file_ref A and caption “before”.
events: An authenticated staff member publishes intake_id I again with file_ref B and caption “after”.
outcomes: The request conflicts and F remains unchanged.
The request is reported as a replay and returns F despite the differences.
F is changed to some or all of the new publication facts.
witness.observer: The staff caller and gallery readers see the result or changed photo.

open_points.subject: audit of first-administrator bootstrap
open_points.text: State 0 R0-07 says the bootstrap command is “never printed, logged or audited,” while M36 says “The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one `staff.create` record.”
open_points.question: Does successful first-administrator bootstrap create an AuditRecord?
options: Create no audit record, as R0-07 requires.
Create one system-actor `staff.create` AuditRecord, as M36 requires.
open_points.default_guess: Create no AuditRecord because R0-07 explicitly defines the bootstrap's disclosure and audit behavior.

witness.initial: The deployment has no staff accounts or audit records.
events: The host operator successfully runs the first-administrator bootstrap command.
outcomes: One active verified administrator exists and the audit log remains empty.
One active verified administrator and one system-actor `staff.create` AuditRecord exist.
witness.observer: The host operator or an audit reader sees whether the audit entry exists.

open_points.subject: ProjectOverview project availability
open_points.text: ProjectOverview originally requires “`project: ProjectContext`,” but the accepted changes say “the project context is absent when Registry cannot be read, and a `project_availability` says so.”
open_points.question: Does ProjectOverview always contain ProjectContext, or does it contain a project availability/context pair like the other components?
options: Require project context and fail or omit the whole overview when Registry cannot be read.
Add `project_availability` and make project context absent unless available.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the accepted change: add project availability and make context conditional.

witness.initial: A permitted project has portal-owned budget and expense data, but Registry is temporarily unavailable.
outcomes: No ProjectOverview can be returned because required `project` cannot be built.
ProjectOverview is returned with project temporarily unavailable and the independently available portal components.
witness.observer: The viewer sees either a failed read or a partial overview.

open_points.subject: BinaryPayload download_name optionality
open_points.text: BinaryPayload declares “`download_name: str | None`,” while the accepted changes say “`download_name` is always present, derived from the object kind and id.”
open_points.question: May an authorized BinaryPayload omit download_name?
options: Allow `download_name = None`.
Require a derived non-null download_name for every payload.

witness.initial: An authorized expense document exists in binary storage.
events: A permitted caller downloads the document.
outcomes: The BinaryPayload may contain no download name.
The BinaryPayload always contains the derived document-and-id download name.
witness.observer: The HTTP adapter and downloader see whether a filename is available.

open_points.subject: hidden photos in the viewer gallery
open_points.text: M35 stores `client_visible`, but `PhotoView` has no visibility field and the PhotoView section states only its fields and gallery order; unlike the expense-document projection, it never says whether a viewer listing excludes hidden photos.
open_points.question: When `ProgressPhoto.client_visible` is false, is that photo absent from the viewer's photo list or present as metadata with only its binary blocked?
options: Omit hidden photos from the viewer gallery.
Include their PhotoView metadata but refuse their binary downloads.
open_points.default_guess: Omit hidden photos from the viewer gallery.

witness.initial: Project P has one active viewer grant and one ProgressPhoto with `client_visible=false`.
events: The viewer reads P's photo gallery.
outcomes: The gallery is empty because the hidden photo is filtered out.
The gallery contains the hidden photo's date, caption and section metadata, although its binary cannot be downloaded.
witness.observer: The viewer sees whether the hidden photo is disclosed in the gallery.
